excluded.authentik: authentik needs a database wired to it and a public URL. Its README shows how to set them up.
excluded.ciso-assistant: CISO Assistant needs a database wired to it and a public URL. Its README shows how to set them up.
excluded.fleet: Fleet needs MySQL, Valkey and a setup step after the first apply. Its README shows how to set them up.
excluded.flux: Flux installs onto a k3s cluster and syncs from your Git repository, so it needs both first. Its README shows how.
excluded.helm: Helm's releases go onto a Kubernetes cluster, so it needs one first. Its README shows how.
excluded.istio: Istio installs onto a k3s cluster, so it needs that cluster first. Its README shows how.
excluded.kubeadm: kubeadm has control planes and workers, two kinds of host. Its README shows how to set them up.
excluded.microshift: MicroShift turns the whole box into an OpenShift node, with its router on 80 and 443. Give it a host of its own and follow its README.
excluded.proxmox: Proxmox turns a Debian host into a hypervisor. Give it a machine of its own and follow its README.
excluded.rancher: Rancher needs a k3s cluster at a version it supports. Its README shows how to set one up.

conflicts.reason: both are a MySQL server on port 3306, and their packages replace each other
circuit-firewall has no rule for VRRP, so every host would claim the floating address
circuit-docker and circuit-kubeadm install their own containerd
circuit-nagios takes over the host's Apache

hints.apache: Name a virtual host and give it a folder to serve or an app to proxy to.
hints.certbot: Its standalone method needs port 80 free. With a web server on the host, set method to webroot or nginx.
hints.cockpit: Logs in with the server's own passwords, so the firewall keeps 9090 to your own network.
hints.couchdb: Listens on 127.0.0.1:5984, for a proxy such as Caddy in front.
hints.firewall: Keeps SSH open, then opens the ports your other picks listen on. The README it writes lists each one.
hints.forgejo: Keeps its data in SQLite and listens on 127.0.0.1:3000, for a proxy such as Caddy in front. Its README shows PostgreSQL.
hints.github-runner: Needs a registration token from the repository's runner settings. You set it as a secret when you run it, and the README says where to get one.
hints.gitlab: Wants a host with 8 GB of memory, and keeps ports 80, 443, 8080, 9090 and 9100 for itself.
hints.gitlab-runner: The runner token comes from GitLab's runner settings. The docker executor needs docker on the host too.
hints.grafana: Listens on 127.0.0.1:3000 unless you set http_addr.
hints.haproxy: Doesn't open the ports your frontends use. Add them to the firewall yourself.
hints.infisical: Brings PostgreSQL and Valkey along and points Infisical at them. Use letters and digits for both passwords, since they go into URLs. Listens on 127.0.0.1:8080, for a proxy in front.
hints.jenkins: Listens on 127.0.0.1:8080, for a proxy such as Caddy in front.
hints.keepalived: Give it two or more hosts on the same network.
hints.keycloak: Listens on 127.0.0.1:8080 and keeps its data in a file meant for trials. Its README shows PostgreSQL.
hints.langfuse: Brings PostgreSQL and Valkey along and points Langfuse at them. Runs ClickHouse and MinIO beside it on ports 8123, 9000 and 9002, and wants about 4 GB of memory. Listens on 127.0.0.1:3000.
hints.litellm: Brings PostgreSQL along and points LiteLLM at it. Use letters and digits for the password, since it goes into a URL. Add your models and API keys in main.tf afterwards; the README shows how.
hints.lldap: Listens on 127.0.0.1 only, for a proxy in front.
hints.matrix: Listens on 127.0.0.1:8008 for a proxy in front. server_name can never change once Synapse has started.
hints.monitoring: Runs on Docker, so circuit-docker comes with it. On Rocky Linux, Cockpit can hold port 9090.
hints.mssql: x86-64 only. Read Microsoft's licence terms before you tick accept_eula. The sa password is a secret you set when you run it.
hints.n8n: Listens on 127.0.0.1:5678 for a proxy in front. Set public_url, or its webhook links point at localhost.
hints.netdata: The dashboard listens on 127.0.0.1:19999. Open an SSH tunnel to see it.
hints.openldap: Listens on 127.0.0.1:389 only. Set ldap_address to serve other hosts.
hints.openwebui: Listens on 127.0.0.1:8080 and talks to Ollama on the same host, so pick ollama too, or set openai_base_url.
hints.otelcol: Doesn't open 4317 or 4318. For a gateway, add them to the firewall yourself.
hints.php: Runs PHP-FPM on a Unix socket. Pick nginx or Apache too, and point it at the socket as the README shows.
hints.presidio: Answers on 127.0.0.1:5001 and 5002, for apps on the same host.
hints.prometheus: On Rocky Linux, Cockpit can hold port 9090, and Prometheus won't start beside it.
hints.wireguard: Give it two or more hosts. Each one peers with the others.
hints.zeek: Set interface to the network card Zeek should watch.
hints.k3s: Set TF_VAR_k3s_token to something like the output of openssl rand -hex 32, and keep it the same for the life of the cluster.
hints.velociraptor: Set TF_VAR_velociraptor_client_nonce to something like the output of openssl rand -hex 16, and keep it the same for the life of the deployment. The GUI listens on the server itself, so reach it through an SSH tunnel or a proxy.
hints.freeipa: The installer takes about ten minutes. Pass the same passwords on every plan as well as every apply. The README explains why.
hints.zabbix: The frontend listens on the server itself, on 127.0.0.1:8080, so reach it through an SSH tunnel or a proxy. Sign in as Admin with your admin password.
hints.cloudflared: Create the tunnel in the Cloudflare dashboard and set TF_VAR_cloudflared_tunnel_token to its token.
hints.trivy: Its vulnerability database takes 1.6 to 3.1 GB of disk. Reports stay on the host.
hints.cinc: Put your cookbooks on the host yourself and point repo_path at them. Set run_list to say which to run.
hints.wazuh: Set the three passwords as TF_VAR_ values. Nothing here makes a host or company compliant.
hints.nomad: Nomad is under the BUSL licence, not open source, and the circuit's README explains what that means. Set TF_VAR_nomad_gossip_key to the output of nomad operator gossip keyring generate. ACLs are on, so run nomad acl bootstrap yourself after the first apply.
hints.nagios: The web interface listens on the host itself, so reach it through an SSH tunnel or a proxy.
hints.selenium: The Grid has no login, so it stays on the host itself. Reach it through an SSH tunnel.
hints.zap: Only scan what you're allowed to. Scans are passive unless you set active_scan.
hints.containerd: This installs containerd alone, with no network config for pods. Its README covers what's left to you.
hints.kotlin: It comes with circuit-java, since the compiler needs a Java on the PATH.

k3s.label: Servers
k3s.oddWhy: embedded etcd loses quorum with two, so one or three is the usual choice.
k3s.help: Run the control plane and embedded etcd. The first name in sorted order starts the cluster.

k3s.label: Agents
k3s.help: Run your workloads and join through the first server. Leave it empty for servers only.

freeipa.label: Server
freeipa.help: Runs the FreeIPA server. It's named <name>.<domain>, so pick the name with that in mind.

freeipa.label: Clients
freeipa.help: Hosts to enrol. They can also run other circuits from this build.

velociraptor.label: Server
velociraptor.help: Runs the Velociraptor server and its GUI.

velociraptor.label: Clients
velociraptor.help: Hosts that report to the server. They can also run other circuits from this build.

zabbix.label: Server
zabbix.help: Runs the Zabbix server, its frontend and the PostgreSQL database they need.

zabbix.label: Agents
zabbix.help: Hosts to run Zabbix agent 2 on. They can also run other circuits from this build, and the server can be one of them.

wazuh.label: Server
wazuh.help: Runs the manager, indexer and dashboard. Wazuh asks for 4 vCPUs, 8 GiB of memory and 50 GB of disk.

wazuh.label: Agents
wazuh.help: Hosts that report to the server. They can also run other circuits from this build, but not the server, whose packages clash with the agent.

nomad.label: Servers
nomad.oddWhy: they vote on a leader, so one or three is the usual choice.
nomad.help: Run the Nomad servers. They need to reach each other, so a private network is best.

nomad.label: Clients
nomad.help: Run your jobs. Leave it empty for servers only.
